name: Shaphan
overview: Shaphan was a male scribe serving King Josiah, noted for his role in the religious reforms during Josiah's reign. He was entrusted with the important task of overseeing the repair of the house of the Lord. His work as a scribe placed him in a position of influence during a pivotal time of spiritual renewal in Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphan means 'rock badger,' a proper name mentioned in 2 Kings 22:3. This name does not appear to have been given by God but identifies him distinctly in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Shaphan had a son named Azaliah, as explicitly stated in 2 Kings 22:3. He is also inferred to be the father of Ahikam (2 Kings 22:12) and Gemariah (Jeremiah 36:10), suggesting a family involved in significant biblical events. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphan's significance lies in his faithful service as a scribe during King Josiah's reign, particularly in connection with the restoration of the temple and the rediscovery of the Book of the Law. His role in reporting and facilitating these reforms highlights his obedience to God's commands through the king's leadership. Through his work, Shaphan contributed to a critical revival of covenant faithfulness in Judah.
